name: IR2184STRPBF
title: 600 V half-bridge gate driver with single input and shutdown
summary: The IR2184 and IR21844 drive the two N-channel MOSFETs or IGBTs of a half bridge from one logic input, with a bootstrapped high side channel that floats up to 600 V. An active-low shutdown input turns both outputs off. The IR2184 has a fixed 400 ns deadtime; the 14-pin IR21844 adds a separate logic ground and a resistor-programmed deadtime of 0.4 to 5 µs. Outputs source 1.9 A and sink 2.3 A typical, and both supplies have undervoltage lockout.

circuits.title: Typical connection, IR2184
circuits.description: One half bridge of N-channel MOSFETs on a rail of up to 600 V. VCC feeds the chip and, through the bootstrap diode D1, the bootstrap capacitor C2 between VB and VS, which supplies the high side driver. C1 bypasses VCC to COM. HO and LO drive the gates through R1 and R2. COM, the low side source and the rail capacitor C3 share one ground. The high side source (VS) and the low side drain come out to two separate load terminals.

circuits.title: Typical connection, IR21844
circuits.description: The 14-pin version in the same half bridge. Logic ground VSS is a pin of its own, with C1 bypassing VCC to VSS and RDT from DT to VSS setting the deadtime. VCC also reaches the bootstrap diode D1, with C4 bypassing it to COM; C2 between VB and VS supplies the high side driver. HO and LO drive the gates through R1 and R2; COM, the low side source and the rail capacitor C3 share one ground. The high side source and the low side drain come out to two separate load terminals.

operation.text: A single logic input sets both outputs: with IN high, HO is on and LO off; with IN low, LO is on and HO off. Cross-conduction prevention logic keeps the two outputs from being on together, and a deadtime separates each turn-off from the opposite turn-on. Pulling SD low forces both HO and LO off whatever IN does; when SD returns high the outputs follow IN again.

The IR2184 has a fixed internal deadtime, 400 ns typical (280 to 520 ns). On the IR21844 a resistor from DT to VSS programs it: with DT tied to VSS (RDT = 0) it is the same 400 ns, and with RDT = 200 kΩ it is 5 µs typical (4 to 6 µs). The programmable range is 0.4 to 5 µs. The deadtime is the same in both directions, LO-off to HO-on and HO-off to LO-on, to within 50 ns at RDT = 0 and 600 ns at 200 kΩ.

The high side channel floats on VS and is built for bootstrap supply. It runs with VS up to +600 V, withstands negative transients on VS and is dV/dt immune; the allowable VS slew is 50 V/ns. Its logic works for VS from -5 V to +600 V; between -5 V and -VBS the output state is held.

VCC and the floating supply VBS each run from 10 to 20 V, and both have undervoltage lockout. The rising threshold is 8.9 V typical (8.0 to 9.8 V), the falling threshold 8.2 V typical (7.4 to 9.0 V), and the hysteresis 0.7 V typical (0.3 V minimum).

IN and SD accept 3.3 V and 5 V logic, CMOS or LSTTL: a high is 2.7 V or more and a low 0.8 V or less over VCC from 10 to 20 V. Each input is clamped internally by a 5.2 V zener. On the IR21844 the logic ground VSS may sit up to 5 V either side of the power ground COM.

The output buffers source at least 1.4 A (1.9 A typical) and sink at least 1.8 A (2.3 A typical) in short pulses, and are designed to keep driver cross-conduction low. The gate driver has a reduced di/dt for noise immunity. Turn-on and turn-off delays of the two channels are matched, within 90 ns at turn-on and 40 ns at turn-off.
The parts are monolithic high-voltage ICs in latch-immune CMOS. They drive N-channel power MOSFETs or IGBTs, one on the high side and one on the low side of a half bridge.
